import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type (boxplot)
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', ax=axes[0, 0], palette='viridis')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Camera Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
axes[0, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price colored by 4K video capability (scatter plot)
scatter = axes[0, 1].scatter(df['megapixels'], df['price_usd'], 
                            c=df['has_video_4k'], cmap='coolwarm', 
                            alpha=0.6, s=50, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Megapixels vs Price (Colored by 4K Video Capability)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Create custom legend for 4K video capability
legend_elements = [plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#1f77b4', 
                             markersize=10, label='No 4K Video'),
                   plt.Line2D([0], [0], marker='o', color='w', markerfacecolor='#d62728', 
                             markersize=10, label='Has 4K Video')]
axes[0, 1].legend(handles=legend_elements, title='4K Video', loc='upper left')

# 3. Camera count by body type (bar plot)
body_type_counts = df['body_type'].value_counts()
bars = axes[1, 0].bar(body_type_counts.index, body_type_counts.values, color=sns.color_palette('husl', len(body_type_counts)))
axes[1, 0].set_title('Camera Count by Body Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
axes[1, 0].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Add value labels on bars
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[1, 0].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 5,
                   f'{int(height)}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

# 4. Average price by brand (top 10 brands)
brand_price_avg = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)
bars2 = axes[1, 1].bar(range(len(brand_price_avg)), brand_price_avg.values, 
                      color=sns.color_palette('rocket', len(brand_price_avg)))
axes[1, 1].set_title('Top 10 Brands by Average Camera Price', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Brand', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_xticks(range(len(brand_price_avg)))
axes[1, 1].set_xticklabels(brand_price_avg.index, rotation=45)
axes[1, 1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Add value labels on bars
for i, bar in enumerate(bars2):
    height = bar.get_height()
    axes[1, 1].text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + 50,
                   f'${height:,.0f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10)

# Adjust layout and add overall title
plt.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
plt.close()
